spec.prompt: A route registered with an invalid logLevel (for example fastify.get('/log', { logLevel: 'invalid' }, handler) on a Fastify instance created with logger: true) is accepted silently. Validate the route's logLevel when the route is registered: if it is not one of the logger's levels, or is not a string, registration must throw a new Fastify error FST_ERR_ROUTE_LOG_LEVEL_INVALID, exported with the other error codes in lib/errors.js. It is a TypeError with statusCode 500 and the message template "Log level for '%s:%s' route must be a valid logger level. Received: '%s'" (method, url, the received value), so the example throws "Log level for 'GET:/log' route must be a valid logger level. Received: 'invalid'". A null logLevel is treated as omitted (no error), and valid levels such as 'debug' are accepted. Adding the error code changes the error count checked in test/internals/errors.test.js; update that expected count.
spec.requirement: Route registration validates opts.logLevel against logger.levels.values when the logger has levels: a value that is not a string, or not a known level, throws FST_ERR_ROUTE_LOG_LEVEL_INVALID (code 'FST_ERR_ROUTE_LOG_LEVEL_INVALID', name 'FastifyError', TypeError, statusCode 500, message template "Log level for '%s:%s' route must be a valid logger level. Received: '%s'" formatted with method, url and the value). null and '' are treated as omitted. Valid levels register normally and the route serves requests.
spec.adjudication_rules: Score pass only if every hidden check passes. No partial credit.

provenance.author: Claude (QB developer side; dev screen, harder candidates)
provenance.notes: Real gap in fastify v5.8.5 (an invalid route logLevel is accepted), fixed upstream in 2ae3e1d7 (#6523). The reference is that fix applied to v5.8.5, plus the upstream update of the error count. The hidden suite follows the upstream tests and adds the non-string and valid-level cases the prompt states.
